comments.body:
WHY THE LIVE CLOUD BRIDGE IS NOT HIT: the trigger is an issue MOVING BETWEEN PROJECTS, and this
project's Jira tickets are not moved. That is untriggered conditions, not immunity — the binding is
keyed on a mutable identifier on Cloud exactly as it is on DC.

Retiring my earlier 'pre-existing, not DC-specific, therefore follow-up' framing. It was true and
self-serving. Self-hosted DC admins move projects routinely, so DC raises the probability of the
trigger while the defect itself is shared.

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED — Gerrit change 1136 ("7c26: survive an issue moving project"), commit
431019b17 on branch jira-family-seam. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

WHAT LANDED, against the plan's Approach
 * `BindingStore.record_jira_id(local_id, jira_id)` + `get_jira_id(local_id)` — the capture and the
   accessor, ADDITIVE by construction.
 * `BindingStore.note_absent_or_rekey(jira_key, client)` — on a 404 it re-asks by the immutable
   numeric id; on a hit whose key DIFFERS it re-keys the binding, updates the reverse index in the
   SAME operation, resets the absence counter, persists, and emits a deduped `binding-rekeyed`
   alert. Returns True on a re-key, False when the absence was recorded exactly as before.
 * Module-level `_current_key_by_id(client, jira_id)` — reuses `get_issue_by_rest`, since
   `GET /rest/api/{2,3}/issue/{issueIdOrKey}` accepts an id wherever it accepts a key on BOTH
   deployments. So NO new transport member and no vendor branch was needed — which matters, because
   the DC transport is at 789 LOC against the 800 cap and had 11 lines of headroom.
 * Capture wired at `dispatch_one` create, in the SAME write that records the key, so the id and the
   key never disagree on disk. getattr-guarded so a store predating the member is a no-op rather
   than a persist-floor failure that would skip the create.
 * BOTH 404 paths wired: `outbound_differ._diff_one` (the primary one for a move — a moved issue
   leaves the project-scoped snapshot entirely) and `binding_walk`'s CONFIRMED_404 branch.

AC-BY-AC
 * "binding SURVIVES, re-keyed, test FAILS against current code" ->
   `test_a_moved_issue_keeps_its_binding_and_is_rekeyed`, driven END-TO-END through the real walk.
 * "absence probe does NOT retire an issue reachable by id" ->
   `test_the_absence_probe_does_not_retire_an_issue_reachable_by_id` with GRACE lowered to 1, so a
   single unrecovered 404 would retire.
 * "reverse index updated in the same operation" -> `test_the_reverse_index_follows_the_rekey`, plus
   `test_the_rekey_is_persisted_not_merely_in_memory` (re-read from disk).
 * "legacy bindings keep working, no migration" ->
   `test_a_legacy_binding_without_an_id_still_retires_at_grace`, which also asserts NO lookup is
   attempted when there is no id to ask by.
 * "id fallback NOT attempted while the key resolves" ->
   `test_the_id_fallback_is_not_attempted_while_the_key_resolves`.
 * "Cloud unchanged: no existing jira_key-taking method changes signature or semantics" ->
   `test_no_existing_jira_key_taking_method_changed_signature` pins ten signatures via
   `inspect.signature`. This is WHY the capture is a separate `record_jira_id` rather than a
   parameter on `bind_confirm`/`record_pending_key`.

Two cells beyond the ACs guard the fix's own failure mode — that a recovery could MASK a deletion:
`test_a_genuine_deletion_still_retires_even_with_a_captured_id` and
`test_an_unchanged_key_is_recorded_as_an_absence`. Every unproven case falls THROUGH to the
unchanged bookkeeping.

VERIFICATION
 * 13/13 new tests pass; 294 pass across the neighbouring suites (binding_walk, all of diffing/,
   absence lifecycle, binding_store).
 * MUTATION-CHECKED, three ways: reverting `binding_walk` to the pre-fix `note_absent` fails 4 cells
   with their intended messages; deleting the reverse-index maintenance fails exactly 2; deleting
   the `save()` fails exactly 1.
 * MY OWN ORACLE WAS WRONG FIRST TIME, and I record it because the lesson generalises: the stub
   probe 404'd on EVERY key, so after the re-key it also 404'd the NEW key — which the code
   correctly treats as a real absence and retires. The test was mis-specified, not the fix. The
   probe is now key-aware, matching what a move actually produces, with the reason in its docstring.
 * make lint + make typecheck clean (mypy: 399 files). All four touched modules under the 800 cap:
   binding_store 744, binding_walk 352, dispatch_one 796, outbound_differ 792.

TWO EXISTING TEST STUBS WERE UPDATED, preserving intent. `test_outbound_differ_bound_but_absent.py`
and `test_inbound_differ_bound_but_absent.py` define stub stores with `note_absent` only, so the
differ's new call found nothing and their "absence bumped once" assertions broke. Each stub now
implements `note_absent_or_rekey` delegating to `note_absent` — exactly the real store's degradation
contract when no id is captured — so the assertions keep their original meaning.

WHY outbound_differ WAS REFACTORED (it will look unrelated in the diff, so the reason is here):
that module sits at EXACTLY the locked 800-LOC cap on main, and it deliberately does NOT import the
concrete BindingStore (a documented Protocol boundary), so the wiring had to be local AND cost
lines. Three byte-identical getattr-guarded bookkeeping wrappers (`_note_absent`, `_clear_absent`,
`_set_last_get`) collapse into one `_best_effort(binding_store, member, *args)`. That bought the
lines from real duplication rather than from comments. No test referenced the three by name.

THE [operator-attested] AC — PARTIALLY SETTLED, AND THE UNSETTLED PART IS NOW A KNOWN NEGATIVE
The criterion asks what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns for a MOVED issue on DC 8.17.1.
**It cannot be settled on this harness, and the reason is itself the finding:** a project move is
not performable through the authoritative client. Verified AT RUNTIME (not from docs) against the
installed pycontribs/jira 3.10.5 — it exposes no move member; `move_to_backlog` is Agile-backlog and
`move_version` is versions. DC's move is the UI wizard (`/secure/MoveIssue!default.jspa`, form-token
bound), and this repo forbids hand-rolled REST for DC. So 200-with-new-key vs 301 vs 404 stays open,
and I am recording that rather than picking the answer two research passes disagreed about.

What the live cells DO establish, added to `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`:
 * `test_an_issue_resolves_by_its_immutable_numeric_id` — the fix's load-bearing mechanism: a by-id
   read answers with the issue's CURRENT key on a real instance. Had DC rejected an id here the
   whole fallback would be inert, and inert in the SILENT direction.
 * `test_a_deleted_issue_fails_by_key_AND_by_id_so_deletions_are_not_masked` — the live counterpart
   of the unit cell above.
These need a harness run to report; that evidence will be recorded here before this ticket closes.

The fix was deliberately designed to be correct under ALL THREE readings of the unsettled question,
which is exactly why it did not have to wait for the answer.

LIVE DC HARNESS EVIDENCE for 7c26's two new live cells — they RAN and PASSED.

RUN: GitHub Actions run 30682512839 (workflow external-integration.yml, --ref main, dispatched
after 7c26 merged as 08b47eb78e).
JOB: "jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)" — job id 91322195258 — SUCCESS.
RESULT LINE: `[jira-live-canary] collected=19 executed=19 skipped=0` / `19 passed in 16.73s`.

THE TWO CELLS THIS TICKET ADDED, both in tests/external/live_jira_dc/:
  * test_an_issue_resolves_by_its_immutable_numeric_id — PASSED
  * test_a_deleted_issue_fails_by_key_AND_by_id_so_deletions_are_not_masked — PASSED

WHY THAT COUNT IS THE PROOF rather than the bare "success". The previous fully-green DC harness
run (30662366152) reported collected=17 executed=17 skipped=0. This run reports 19/19 with
skipped=0. So the delta is exactly this ticket's two cells, and — because skipped=0 — neither was
silently skipped, which is the failure mode that matters for live cells (a missing harness makes
them skip rather than fail, and a skipped live cell is not evidence of anything). Both executed
against a real, ephemeral Jira Data Center instance and both passed.

ONE JOB IN THE SAME RUN FAILED AND IT IS NOT OURS. "external integration (live services)"
(job 91322195282) failed in tests/external/test_execution_mode_live.py — the live LLM workflow
tests (`assert res["status"] == "succeeded"` on a `live_single_turn` workflow run, and
`verdict["coverage"].get("llm_ran") is True`). That is the LLM execution-mode suite, not the Jira
DC harness; it touches no adapter, transport, or binding code. Recorded explicitly so the run's
overall red does not later get misread as a DC failure — counts are not causes, and neither is a
run-level conclusion.

WHAT REMAINS UNSETTLED, unchanged and already documented on this ticket: a real project MOVE is
not performable through pycontribs/jira 3.10.5 (verified at RUNTIME — there is no move member;
`move_to_backlog` is Agile and `move_version` is versions), and DC's move is a UI wizard. So what
`GET /issue/{oldKey}` returns after a genuine move stays OPEN. The live cells above cover what IS
checkable on this harness — resolution by the immutable numeric id, and that a deleted issue fails
by key AND by id so a deletion cannot masquerade as a re-key. The remediation (key on the numeric
id, re-ask by id on a 404) does not depend on which of 200/301/404 a moved key returns, which is
why it was safe to land ahead of that answer.

compiled_state.description:
# Bindings key on the Jira KEY, which changes when an issue moves project

## Context / Problem

A Jira issue's KEY changes when it is moved between projects; its numeric `id` never does. Old keys
are normally stacked in the `moved_issue_key` table so the old key still resolves — but a
Data-Center-specific Atlassian KB documents that third-party apps moving issues via workflow
post-functions, automations or scheduled routines can FAIL to update that table, after which the old
key stops resolving entirely.

rebar's bindings are keyed on the KEY, and pervasively so — not just `get_jira_key`/`get_local_id`,
but the `reverse` index, `note_absent`, `_retire`, `clear_absent` and `set_last_get` all take a
`jira_key`. So a moved issue can silently detach: the binding points at a key that no longer resolves,
the absence probe reads it as gone, and the local ticket is orphaned from an issue that still exists.

**What is NOT established, and must not be built on.** An earlier research pass asserted that
`GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns 200 with a body carrying the NEW key. That was retracted on a
second pass and is unverified: the KB does not state whether a stale key yields 200-with-new-key, 301
or 404. The remediation below is deliberately chosen to be correct under ALL THREE readings, so this
story does not block on settling it — but it is still settled here, as evidence, because two passes
disagreed and the next reader deserves the answer.

## Approach

**Record the numeric `id` alongside the key on every binding, and resolve by `id` when a key lookup
misses — re-keying the binding to the issue's current key when it does.**

This is deliberately ADDITIVE rather than a re-keying of the store, and that choice is the whole
design decision:

* the binding store is SHARED WITH CLOUD. Changing the store's identity from key to id would rewrite
  the `reverse` index and every absence/retirement/last-get path for both vendors — a large blast
  radius on the live Cloud bridge to fix a DC-specific detachment. Additive id-capture leaves every
  existing key-keyed path behaving exactly as today.
* it is correct under all three unresolved readings of what a stale key returns. If the old key still
  resolves (200, with or without the new key in the body) nothing changes and the fallback never
  fires. If it 404s, the id fallback recovers the binding. No detection heuristic depends on the
  unverified behaviour.
* it degrades safely on a store written before this change: an entry with no recorded `id` simply has
  no fallback and behaves exactly as it does today. No migration is required, and the id is captured
  opportunistically on the next successful read of that issue.

Concretely: `bind_confirm` and `record_pending_key` accept and persist an optional `jira_id`; a
`get_jira_id(local_id)` accessor is added; and the absence probe, before concluding an issue is gone,
retries the lookup by recorded `id` and — on a hit whose key differs — updates the binding's key
(maintaining the `reverse` index) and treats the issue as PRESENT rather than absent.

**Rejected: re-keying the binding store on the numeric id.** It is the "cleaner" answer and it is what
the original ticket proposed, but it changes shared Cloud-facing identity semantics, rewrites the
reverse index and every `jira_key`-taking method, and requires a store migration — all to reach the
same end state this achieves additively. If DC experience later shows the fallback firing routinely,
re-keying becomes a justified follow-up with evidence behind it.

**Rejected: detecting a move by parsing the old key's GET response.** That is precisely the mechanism
two research passes disagreed about. Building on it would make the fix depend on unverified behaviour.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py` — persist and expose `jira_id`; re-key on an
  id-resolved move.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — capture the numeric id
  on reads (it is already present in the unwrapped REST payload as `id`).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — the harness experiment recording what a stale key actually returns.

## Testing

* **the binding survives a move** — a fake client where the issue's key changes and the OLD key 404s,
  while the recorded numeric id still resolves: assert the binding is preserved, re-keyed to the new
  key, and NOT retired by the absence probe. This is the defect, so it is asserted end-to-end rather
  than by inspecting the entry.
* **the `reverse` index follows the re-key** — the old key no longer maps to the local id and the new
  one does. A stale reverse entry would re-detach on the next pass.
* **a pre-existing binding with no recorded id** behaves exactly as today (no fallback, no crash),
  so the change is safe on an unmigrated store.
* **the fallback does not fire when the key still resolves** — asserted by a client that fails the
  test if the id lookup is attempted, since a fallback firing on the happy path would double every
  absence probe's cost.
* **live** — record what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns on DC 8.17.1 after a real move,
  as evidence, since two research passes disagreed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a binding whose issue moved project SURVIVES: with the old key 404ing and the recorded numeric
      id resolving, the binding is preserved and re-keyed to the current key, asserted by a test that
      FAILS against the current code
- [ ] the absence probe does NOT retire an issue that is reachable by its recorded id — the specific
      silent detachment this ticket exists to stop
- [ ] the `reverse` index is updated in the same operation as the re-key, asserted, so the old key
      stops resolving to the local id
- [ ] bindings written BEFORE this change (no `jira_id`) continue to work unchanged, with no
      migration step, asserted by a test over a legacy-shaped entry
- [ ] the id fallback is NOT attempted while the key resolves normally, asserted by a client that
      fails if it is called — the happy path must not pay for the recovery path
- [ ] Cloud behaviour is unchanged: no existing `jira_key`-taking method changes signature or
      semantics, verified by reading the diff, since this store is shared
- [ ] [operator-attested] what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns for a moved issue on DC 8.17.1
      (status, and whether the body carries the new key) is RECORDED on this ticket as evidence — two
      research passes disagreed and the answer must stop being folklore. The fix does not depend on
      the answer; this criterion exists to settle it
